This is the kickoff, first of three meetings, for the draft spec on the Defense Information Infrastructure Common Operating Environment XML Services. Let's start with some background."},{"id":"M1:T2","text":"Sure. So XML Services are basically infrastructure services for mission and support applications, built on XML technology. The idea is they hide the vendor-unique ways of doing data access, so applications don't end up depending on physical access models. They also give us data management functions for reaching distributed databases, local and remote, as one of the ways we get interoperability."},{"id":"M1:T3","text":"Can I jump in on required states and modes? Because there's the environmental mode, which is the real-time operations side. That has to react to different degrees of readiness, all the way up to full scale wartime operations—"},{"id":"M1:T4","text":"Sorry, real-time as in live ops?"},{"id":"M1:T5","text":"Yeah, live. So things like crisis planning, where you're using heterogeneous data types and sources, plus transfer capabilities and data management services."},{"id":"M1:T6","text":"Then there's COE compliance. I think XML Services are supposed to be segmented, maybe, I'm not totally sure that's mandatory, but"},{"id":"M1:T7","text":"Okay, go on."},{"id":"M1:T8","text":"and the COE sponsors would have to stick to the compliance level requirements that are described in the I&RTS."},{"id":"M1:T9","text":"For the fixed, static mode, so a base or a data processing megacenter, on-site personnel need to be able to tune the data management services to handle varying workloads and different database sizes. Those workloads and databases are going to change more often, and by more, than what you'd see with deployed units."},{"id":"M1:T10","text":"Do we really need that tuning capability? It's a lot of effort for something that's probably not top priority right now."},{"id":"M1:T11","text":"I'd push back, it really matters to us. I don't want to lose it."},{"id":"M1:T12","text":"I hear you, but given the effort, let's drop it from scope for now and revisit later if needed."},{"id":"M1:T13","text":"Alright. Then in a changing, dynamic environment"},{"id":"M1:T14","text":"Mm-hm."},{"id":"M1:T15","text":"like with deployed units, the workload"},{"id":"M1:T16","text":"Right."},{"id":"M1:T17","text":"and the database sizes might be more predetermined, since the mission is more precise"},{"id":"M1:T18","text":"Got it."},{"id":"M1:T19","text":"and they'd need fewer data management admin capabilities than the fixed environment does. Also, the XS has to be able to redefine or reset the names of connect descriptors to database server instances. Those connect descriptors are fully qualified object names, and they include the address, meaning protocol, host and port, plus the instance name."},{"id":"M1:T20","text":"One more. When communications are degraded, we need to be able to, for example, reset session time-out values if the users hitting the data management services are affected by that degradation. At a minimum, users should be able to define the session time-out values and reset them before a user session gets initialized. What we're really aiming for is the option to change session time values dynamically, based on current communications performance, as identified by what the network management or the DBMS can tell us."}]}
